title: Ex 7.1 (⇒) · If x is even, then 3x + 5 is odd
prompt: Let $x$ be an integer. Exercise 7.1 says $x$ is even if and only if $3x + 5$ is odd. This problem is one direction of that if-and-only-if: prove that if $x$ is even, then $3x + 5$ is odd. Use direct proof. (The converse (⇐) direction is a separate problem.)
answer_format: A structured proof: let, case, expr and witness steps (notes optional). No final answer box.
hints: Write x = 2a with a let step.
3(2a) + 5 = 6a + 5 = 6a + 4 + 1. Take out a factor of 2 from 6a + 4.
solution: Suppose $x$ is even, so $x = 2a$ for some integer $a$.
Then $3x + 5 = 6a + 5 = 2(3a + 2) + 1$, and $3a + 2$ is an integer, so $3x + 5$ is odd. $\blacksquare$
